title: Bread Sauce
subtitle: British spiced white bread and milk sauce for roast chicken
excerpt: Bread sauce is the ancient British sauce for roast chicken: a simple mixture of crustless white bread simmered in milk infused with onion, cloves, and bay leaves, enriched with butter and cream. It is one of the oldest sauces in British cooking, unchanged for centuries, and it is one of the best accompaniments to roast chicken there is.
sourceNotes: Bread sauce appears in British cookbooks from the 16th century. It is one of the oldest surviving English sauces and was the standard accompaniment to roast fowl before gravy became the default. The sauce is particularly traditional at Christmas and Easter with roast chicken or turkey. The technique of infusing milk with aromatics before adding bread is distinctive and gives a flavour unlike any other sauce.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made 2 hours ahead and reheated gently with a splash of milk to loosen.

content.text: The onion is not eaten -- it infuses the milk with its flavour and is removed before the bread is added. Push the cloves into the onion so they are easy to remove later. The bread should be crustless white bread, preferably a day old. The sauce thickens as it sits -- loosen with a splash of milk before serving.

Put {{whole-milk}} milk in a saucepan with {{onion}} onion halves (with {{cloves}} cloves pushed in), {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves, and {{black-peppercorns}} peppercorns. Bring to a bare simmer over low heat. Remove from the heat and leave to infuse for 20 minutes.
Remove the onion, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Return the pan to low heat. Add {{bread-white}} bread pieces and stir as they absorb the milk and the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.

Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter, {{double-cream}} cream, and {{nutmeg}} nutmeg. Season with {{salt-table}} salt. The sauce should be thick but pourable -- add a splash more milk if needed. Serve warm alongside roast chicken.

items.cause: The bread was added too quickly to hot milk, or not stirred enough.
items.fix: Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until smooth. If still lumpy, pass through a sieve. The sauce should be completely smooth and thick.

content.text: Bread sauce is one of the oldest surviving British sauces. It appears in Tudor and Elizabethan cookbooks and was the standard partner for roast birds for centuries. It is particularly associated with Christmas dinner and with the traditional British roast chicken. The sauce has a characteristic comforting, slightly sweet quality from the cloves and onion that no other sauce replicates.
